plainTranslation:
The overlap is there, but you may have noticed it tends to sit unused. You both know the kind of thing you enjoy. You both can picture the good weekend, the nice meal, the small ritual that would make life feel richer. And then the week happens, and the default is routine, distraction, nothing in particular. The taste is shared. The acting on it is what goes missing.

When this works, it is because someone makes the move. One of you books the thing, plans the evening, spends on the experience instead of letting it stay a someday. And it lands, because you already know what the other person enjoys, so the effort almost never misses. The pleasure does not have to be extravagant. It just has to actually happen.

This contact teaches something quietly important. The life you both want does not assemble itself out of good intentions. It gets built in small deliberate choices, the reservation made, the money set aside for the thing that matters, the ordinary evening someone decided to make nice on purpose.

Act on what you both already value. Make the plan instead of imagining it. This connection gets richer every single time one of you turns the shared wanting into something you actually did, rather than something you both agreed would be lovely sometime.
